Which minimum-event alternatives did each method detect?

Reactant → product only; one seed, cap 1000. The same total can describe different bond changes. This viewer compares full sets of broken, formed, strengthened and weakened bonds, merging symmetry-equivalent atom relabelings. All atoms, including H, contribute to the scores.

BrokenFormedStrengthenedWeakened

Diagrams use a projection of the reactant coordinates. Highlighted bonds refer to the displayed representative; a method may encode a symmetry-equivalent relabeling. Atom indices are zero-based. These are candidate bond-edit patterns, not experimentally verified pathways.

How the comparison was checked

AAM uses one seed order, branch cap 1000 and tolerance 1.0. Native XYZ SLAP is shown both without cuts and with the uncut plus every individual reactant-edge deletion in the reactant → product direction. Every pattern is scored on the original full-H WBO matrices: bond presence > 0.2, order-change magnitude > 0.5. This catalogue holds the benchmark's recorded minimum score fixed.

The analysis scans forward AAM terminal witnesses, enumerates SLAP label-family event patterns, and queries the correlated AAM families. “Excluded” requires completed membership checks or completed enumeration. An unfinished enumeration is a lower bound and cannot prove absence. Additional AAM alternatives may exist where enumeration remains incomplete.

The downloadable report includes mappings, compressed-family witnesses, completeness flags, source hashes and independent finite checks. No mapping search or benchmark timing was rerun.
